messages:
Anya: quick design check — updated SLO slider mock: https://redwood.pics/slo-slider-v3.png. Two UX questions: 1) if user drags the SLO slider down to lower latency target (toward tighter SLO) while Burst is ON, should we automatically nudge min capacity up to keep the SLO achievable? 2) when a small GPU pool is selected, should Burst be disabled or just show a warning? want opinions before I iterate copy/layout. Jamal: technically we shouldn't mutate the user's explicit min/max without confirmation. Auto-changing values is surprising. we can compute a "suggested min" and show a one-click affordance: `Apply suggested min` next to the inputs. keeps actions explicit. Matt R: +1 to suggested min CTA. copy idea: CTA label `Apply suggested min` and beneath, helper copy: "Recommended to meet the SLO given current pool and burst settings." If we show a warning for small pools, let's make it soft (yellow) with a link to docs. Rio: layout notes — prefer slider left, numeric min/max inputs to the right in a compact inline group, then burst pill under the inputs. that reduces vertical scanning. also: contrast on the disabled burst state is low in the mock. please bump the border and make the focus ring 3px. keyboard flow: tab goes slider -> min -> max -> burst -> apply suggestion. show stepper arrow keyboard affordances on the inputs. Jamal: implementation note on pool interaction: for some pool types (e.g., tiny-preemptible), we can't actually guarantee burst capacity; so we should disable the `Apply suggested min` CTA and swap to `View suggestion (read-only)` with a tooltip explaining runtime limits. Anya: good call. copy for disabled CTA: `Suggestion unavailable for selected pool` and tooltip: `Selected GPU pool has limited burst capacity; suggestion is advisory only.` thoughts? Matt R: sounds good. small copy tweak: change `Suggestion unavailable` -> `Autoscale suggestion unavailable` (clearer in list views). also can we add a microcopy line under the min/max: `SLO cost estimate: ~$0.12/hr` — approximate cost helps product folks. Rio: accessibility nits: - ensure slider has `aria-labelledby` and `aria-valuetext` describing target and estimated cost. - inputs need `aria-label` and visible label for screen readers. - tooltips must be reachable by keyboard (focusable info icons). I'll add a11y annotations on the next frames. a11y-bot: quick checklist: keyboard operable slider (arrow keys change by step), numeric inputs accept typed values and stepper buttons, focus order matches visual order, ARIA roles: `role=slider`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, plus `aria-describedby` pointing to the helper copy. color contrast: disabled burst pill is 3.2:1 -> bump to at least 4.5:1 for AA. Example snippet: ```html
``` Jamal: I'll add an API flag `suggested_min` and `suggestion_status` (available|unavailable|advisory). frontend will render CTA state accordingly. Anya: can we run a quick A/B? default-off for `Apply suggested min` vs default-on but with a clear banner explaining auto-applied suggestions for new configs. i think default-off is safer. Matt R: agree default-off. A/B only for new configs created in next sprint. action items: Jamal — API + backend check, Rio — a11y frames + contrast updates, Anya — update mock and copy, Matt — draft banner copy. :thumbsup:
